_about: The settings of a Tron bundle in format 2 (MPF-Godot-Packaging platforms/game-bundle-format2.md): the platform draws the form, stores the values and applies each one through its target: a Godot user argument (--name=value), a key of an ini file written before the start, or the MPF hardware set. Source of truth for the bundle; options.json belongs to the format 1 tool.

options.label: Hardware and model
options.help: virtual: no machine, play with the keyboard, free play (Pro). virtual_coins: the same with the factory pricing. virtual_le: the LE's IO. proc: a Multimorphic P-ROC on a Pro's SAM boards. proc_le: on an LE. proc_fiber: a Pro with its ramp light tubes driven (only after the wiring has been checked: docs/hardware.md).

options.label: DMD look
options.help: hd: smooth text and art at the window's size. classic: the ROM's 128x32 dots.

options.label: DMD colour
options.help: HD only. Tron blue, or the original DMD's orange.

options.label: Text font
options.help: HD only. rajdhani is clean, orbitron is Tron style (wider), rom is the ROM's own dot fonts smoothed.

options.label: Text size
options.help: HD only. 1 = capitals as tall as the ROM's. Above 1.1 stacked lines touch. The service menu (ADJUSTMENTS > DISPLAY ADJUSTMENTS) sets it too, and what it saves wins.

options.label: Text glow
options.help: HD only. 0 = none. The service menu sets it too, and what it saves wins.

options.label: Text colour
options.help: HD only. Leave unset for the colour of the DMD colour above.

options.label: Dot-matrix look
options.help: HD only. 0 = off. N = N round dots per DMD dot (2 looks good from 1280 px up).

options.label: Frame rate cap
options.help: Frames per second at most. 30 matches the PuP Pack's videos and keeps the frames steady; 60 for a smoother DMD where the GPU keeps up; 0 = no cap. On a 75 or 144 Hz screen pick 0 or a divisor of its rate (72 on 144 Hz): 30 would judder.

options.label: DMD window size
options.help: WIDTHxHEIGHT, for example 1920x480.

options.label: PuP videos and music
options.help: Off: the original game, ROM music, no extra windows.

options.label: PuP OST music
options.help: Off: the ROM's music, the videos still play.

options.label: Window layout
options.help: split: the backglass at the left as large as the screen allows, the DMD over the topper at the right. stack: the three windows one under the other at the left. manual: each at the screen, position and size of its own section in pup.local.cfg.

options.label: Backglass monitor
options.help: Monitor index of the backglass window (0 = the main one). With the split layout the DMD and topper join it in the right column when they are on the same monitor.

options.label: DMD monitor
options.help: Monitor index of the DMD window. Another monitor than the backglass's: the DMD fills it (a second screen in the backbox). Same monitor: it sits in the column at the right of the backglass.

options.label: Topper monitor
options.help: Monitor index of the topper window; another monitor than the backglass's: it fills that monitor.

options.label: DMD size in the PuP window
options.help: cycles: a smaller DMD with the light cycles round it. full: a real DMD's size, no light cycles. The service menu (PUP DMD SIZE) chooses too, and wins.

options.label: DMD display
options.help: window: its own window. external: none on screen, a PIN2DMD or ZeDMD shows it. stacked: under the backglass videos, in the backglass window. overlay: over the bottom of the backglass videos. stacked and overlay keep one full screen window (much faster on a Raspberry Pi 4). The platform's DMD output (a PIN2DMD or ZeDMD) always means external.

options.label: DMD background
options.help: lightcycles: a live 3D light cycle chase round the DMD (too heavy for a Raspberry Pi 4). frame: the PuP Pack's DMD panel art. none: black.

options.label: Encrypted provider key
options.help: As Scorbit gave it. Never shown again after it is set.

options.label: Server
options.help: The service menu's SCORBIT SERVER chooses too, and wins.
